name: Acne & Breakouts
productTypes: Salicylic acid (BHA) 2% cleanser or leave-on treatment

am: Wash with a gentle cleanser for 30-60 seconds, lukewarm water
Apply a lightweight non-comedogenic moisturizer
Finish with SPF 30+ sunscreen (this step is non-negotiable)
pm: Double cleanse if you wore sunscreen or sweated: oil-based cleanser first, then regular cleanser
Apply salicylic acid treatment 2-3 nights per week on clean dry skin
Moisturize — even oily skin needs a light gel moisturizer
Use benzoyl peroxide or hydrocolloid patches as spot treatment only

signs: Recurring pimples, whiteheads, or blackheads on the face
Clogged pores or visible congestion on nose, chin, or forehead
Post-acne marks or dark spots after spots heal
Breakouts that correlate with stress, poor sleep, or diet changes
weekly: Use a salicylic acid exfoliant 2-3 times per week (not daily)
Apply a clay mask once per week if skin is very oily
Wash pillowcases twice per week — fabric bacteria worsens breakouts
Deep-clean phone screen weekly; it presses bacteria against the cheek
whatToAvoid: Picking, squeezing, or popping spots (causes scarring and spreads bacteria)
Over-washing or scrubbing hard — it strips the barrier and increases oil production
Layering many new products at once; introduce one new product per week
Heavy, oily, or comedogenic products that clog pores
Toothpaste, lemon, or home scrubs as spot treatments

name: Redness & Irritation
productTypes: Mineral SPF 30+ (zinc oxide based, tinted if you prefer)

am: Cleanse with a gentle cream or milk cleanser — no foaming formulas
Apply niacinamide or centella serum to damp skin
Moisturize with a ceramide-rich cream
Apply mineral sunscreen last
pm: Cleanse gently — double cleanse only if wearing heavy sunscreen
Apply azelaic acid 3-4 nights per week for redness and uneven tone
Follow with a rich ceramide moisturizer
Use a soothing mask on irritated days if needed

signs: Facial skin that looks flushed or pink even at rest
Skin feels warm, tight, or stings after washing
Red patches on cheeks, nose, or around the mouth
Reacts easily to new products, weather changes, or hot showers
weekly: Do a soothing oat or aloe mask once per week
Review your products weekly and remove anything with added fragrance or alcohol
Track triggers (spicy food, alcohol, heat, stress) in a note for 2-3 weeks
whatToAvoid: Physical scrubs and exfoliating brushes
Hot water on the face — use lukewarm only
Fragrance, essential oils, and drying alcohols in products
Harsh acids (high-strength glycolic peels, strong retinoids) while irritated
Over-exfoliating: redness-prone skin rarely needs more than 1-2 exfoliation sessions per week

name: Dullness & Uneven Tone
productTypes: Gentle exfoliating cleanser (PHA or low-strength AHA)
Vitamin C serum (10-15% L-ascorbic acid or derivative)
Kojic acid serum (brightening agent for hyperpigmentation and de-tanning)
Azelaic acid 10% serum or cream (fades dark marks and evens tone)
Gentle chemical exfoliant (lactic or mandelic acid)
Broad-spectrum SPF 50+ PA++++ sunscreen — two finger-lengths for face, ears, and neck; reapply every 2-3 hours outdoors

am: Cleanse with a gentle cleanser
Apply vitamin C serum (wait 30-60 seconds before next step)
Moisturize
Apply SPF 30+ — UV is the top cause of dullness and dark marks
pm: Cleanse thoroughly
Apply a gentle chemical exfoliant 2-3 nights per week (alternate with rest nights)
On non-exfoliant nights, use niacinamide serum for tone evening
Moisturize well to lock in hydration

signs: Skin looks tired, gray, or lacks glow even with enough sleep
Uneven skin tone or visible dark marks and patches
Makeup or sunscreen sits unevenly on the skin
Skin feels rough or looks flaky up close
weekly: Exfoliate with a gentle chemical exfoliant 2-3 times per week — never daily at first
Do a hydrating sheet or gel mask once per week
Get 20-30 minutes of morning daylight for circadian and skin health
De-tan order of operations: strict sun protection FIRST to stop new melanin, then fade existing tan with brightening agents — sunscreen is what keeps the tan from returning
Wash makeup brushes or sponges weekly
whatToAvoid: Skipping sunscreen — UV darkens marks and keeps skin looking dull
Mixing vitamin C with strong acids in the same routine (irritation risk)
Over-exfoliating to chase a glow — barrier damage looks duller, not brighter
Smoking and excess alcohol, which visibly age skin and flatten tone

name: Excess Oil & Shine
productTypes: Oil-free SPF 30+ gel or fluid sunscreen

am: Cleanse with a gel or foaming cleanser
Apply niacinamide serum
Use an oil-free gel moisturizer — skipping moisturizer makes oiliness worse
Apply oil-free SPF 30+ sunscreen
pm: Cleanse thoroughly — double cleanse on sweaty days
Use salicylic acid treatment 2-3 nights per week
Apply lightweight gel moisturizer
Blot excess oil during the day instead of re-washing

signs: Face looks shiny within 1-3 hours of washing
Pores look large, especially on the nose and cheeks
Makeup or sunscreen slides off or breaks up quickly
Frequent blackheads or congestion in the T-zone
weekly: Apply a clay mask once per week to draw out excess sebum
Use salicylic acid exfoliant 2-3 times per week
Carry blotting papers for midday touch-ups instead of washing again
Wash pillowcases twice per week
whatToAvoid: Harsh, stripping cleansers — they trigger rebound oil production
Skipping moisturizer because skin is oily
Washing your face more than twice daily
Heavy creams, oils, and comedogenic ingredients
Touching your face throughout the day

name: Dryness & Dehydration
productTypes: Occlusive balm or petrolatum for very dry nights

am: Cleanse with a cream cleanser or just lukewarm water on mild days
Apply hyaluronic acid serum to damp skin
Layer a hydrating toner if skin still feels tight
Seal with a rich moisturizer, then SPF 30+
pm: Cleanse with an oil-based or cream cleanser
Apply hyaluronic acid serum to damp skin
Apply squalane or a rich ceramide cream
On very dry nights, finish with a thin occlusive layer to seal everything in

signs: Skin feels tight, rough, or itchy after washing
Visible flaking or ashy patches, especially around the mouth and brows
Fine lines look more pronounced when skin is dry
Makeup clings to dry patches or looks cakey
weekly: Do a deeply hydrating mask once per week
Exfoliate very gently once per week at most — dry skin over-exfoliates easily
Run a humidifier in your bedroom if the air is dry
Review diet and water intake; dehydration shows on skin quickly
whatToAvoid: Foaming or gel cleansers with sulfates
Long hot showers — keep water lukewarm and showers short
Alcohol-based toners and astringents
Skipping moisturizer or using too little of it
Heavily fragranced products

name: Under-Eye Darkness & Puffiness
productTypes: Cooling eye masks or chilled spoons
SPF for the eye area (sunscreen applied carefully around eyes)
Color-correcting concealer (peach tone) for daytime coverage

am: Apply a caffeine-based eye cream with gentle tapping — never rub
If puffy, use a chilled spoon or cooling mask for 5 minutes
Apply sunscreen around (not in) the eye area
Concealer only if needed, in natural light
pm: Remove all makeup and sunscreen gently — leftover residue darkens the area
Apply a vitamin C or peptide eye cream
Sleep on your back with your head slightly elevated to reduce morning puffiness

signs: Visible darkness or shadowing under the eyes in normal light
Puffiness or bags that are worse in the morning
Eyes look tired even after a full night of sleep
Thin skin showing bluish or brownish tones under the eyes
weekly: Track sleep hours — most under-eye darkness is sleep-related
Reduce salty late-night meals, which worsen morning puffiness
Get 20-30 minutes of daylight to regulate sleep quality
Limit late-night screen time, which strains eyes and disrupts sleep
whatToAvoid: Rubbing or pulling the under-eye skin — it thins and darkens it further
Sleeping face-down, which increases morning puffiness
Relying only on creams while sleeping under 6 hours
Harsh actives (strong retinoids, high-strength acids) directly under the eyes without guidance
